title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure, and it is deliberate rather than accidental. Generative AI is used to clone a voice from public social media video, to spoof a phone number, to fabricate photographs, and to gather details about a victim's personal relationships. The identity being copied here belongs to an immigration attorney in South Florida, and the people approached are immigrants seeking legal help. The technology does not fail on its own, it is pointed at a trusted professional identity and used to make a stranger sound like that person.

The point of failure sits in the contact channel itself. A call or a social media message arrives with nothing in it that the recipient can check against an independent source, and the reporting notes that banks now describe these impersonation attempts as harder to detect. The checks identified in the coverage are verification through a phone number the recipient already knows, a prearranged code word, and confirmation with the attorney's office directly. Each of those works by leaving the channel the scammer controls.

What is not established is any legal finding. These reports describe complaints, losses and warnings, not arrests, charges or verdicts, and no individual is named as responsible. The loss figures come from the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report and from victim complaints, so they record what was reported rather than what was proven, and the reporting itself states that many victims never report at all.

summary:
Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to create convincing deepfakes and voice clones for scams across Georgia and South Florida. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans lost nearly $893 million to AI-enabled scams last year. Notable victims include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints with $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia had 71 complaints totaling $10.4 million in losses, though the actual numbers are likely much higher since many victims don't report being scammed.

Scammers use generative AI to clone voices from social media videos, spoof phone numbers, create fake photographs, and research personal relationships to make their schemes more believable. Common scams include grandparent scams using voice imitation, romance schemes, and emergency requests. Banks warn that these impersonation attempts are becoming harder to detect. Experts recommend establishing code words with family members, verifying urgent requests through known phone numbers, never sending money based on phone calls alone, and reporting suspected scams to law enforcement or the FBI.
